# ImageImport

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Editing` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public static class ImageImport
```

Turning a picture somebody drew elsewhere into something a layer can hold.

## Remarks

Two kinds of layer take an image two different ways, and the difference is the whole reason this is one place rather than two. A **Custom** layer keeps every channel: the art IS the art, composited untouched. A **Dynamic** or **Static** layer is a value-map, which stores lightness only and is colorized at generation time — so foreign art has to be collapsed to one channel first, and whatever color it had is gone.

It lives in Core because two screens now do it: the editor replaces one variant's raster from a file, and importing a picture as a whole new layer builds the first one. Two copies of "what happens to a color image on a value-map layer" is how the same PNG comes to import differently depending on which button was pressed.

### HasColor(Image&lt;Rgba32&gt;) { #m-hascolor-sixlabors-imagesharp-image-sixlabors-imagesha-18a363 }

```csharp
public static bool HasColor(Image<Rgba32> image);
```

Whether any pixel carries color — channels that are not all equal.

**Parameters**

- `image` (`Image<Rgba32>`) - The picture to examine.

**Returns.** True when at least one visible pixel is not gray.

**Remarks**

What a value-map import WARNS about: the conversion is lossy exactly when this is true, and silently lossless when it is not. A fully transparent pixel cannot show color, so it is skipped — otherwise a stray colored pixel under zero alpha would warn about art that looks identical before and after.

### ToValueMap(Image&lt;Rgba32&gt;) { #m-tovaluemap-sixlabors-imagesharp-image-sixlabors-images-032d59 }

```csharp
public static ValueMap ToValueMap(Image<Rgba32> image);
```

The value-map a picture becomes on a Dynamic or Static layer.

**Parameters**

- `image` (`Image<Rgba32>`) - The source picture. It is NOT modified.

**Returns.** Its lightness, as a value-map.

**Remarks**

**Desaturated FIRST, rather than handing the color image straight to [`ValueMap.FromImage()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.ValueMap.md#m-fromimage-sixlabors-imagesharp-image-sixlabors-imagesh-0fdee0).** That reads the RED channel — exact and lossless for its real job, round-tripping a layer's own already-grayscale PNG, and arbitrary for foreign art: pure green would import as pure BLACK and pure red as pure WHITE, though both read as mid-bright to the eye. `Grayscale()` is ITU-R BT.709 luminance, so R==G==B afterwards and `FromImage`'s own contract is left exactly as it was. Alpha is untouched either way.
